facts.fact_text: On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women's Day celebrations in the city of Malatya.
The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, was a spokesperson for the Women's Democratic Platform.
The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, told the police chief that the applicants were exercising their constitutional right.
The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, told the police chief that the applicable legislation required no prior permission for the gathering.
On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women's Day celebrations in Malatya, according to the Government's submissions.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, a group comprising hundreds of police officers formed a cordon around the crowd.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, the police chief warned the participants that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.
Police officers dragged a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers sprayed the crowds with tear gas.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers hit some of the crowd, including four of the applicants.
The second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, was sprayed with tear gas during the events of 8 March 2005.
The four arrested applicants were taken to a police station on 8 March 2005.
Later on 8 March 2005, the four arrested applicants were released from police custody.
According to the Government's submissions, police officers put a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles by force on 8 March 2005.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, the police chief warned the participants that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.
According to the Government's submissions, a police chief warned the participants on 8 March 2005 that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.
In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that the applicants had gathered in the area without having sought prior permission.

The criminal proceedings brought on 8 March 2005 against the four applicants and the five other arrested persons were for insulting the police officers and contravening the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
According to the Government's submissions, the demonstrations at the International Women's Day celebrations in Malatya on 8 March 2005 hindered the flow of traffic.
According to the Government's submissions, police officers requested the demonstrators to hold their demonstrations without impeding the circulation of traffic on 8 March 2005.

According to the Government's submissions, the police chief told the participants on 8 March 2005 that they could carry on with their demonstration on the pavement and walk in an orderly manner without violating public order.

According to the Government's submissions, the police chief made several unsuccessful attempts to tell the participants that the manner in which they were conducting their demonstration was unlawful because they were impeding the flow of traffic.

According to the Government's submissions, the police chief told the participants that they could leave their placards — which were too large — and walk on the pavement, and that the placards would be returned to them later.
According to the Government's submissions, the group of demonstrators insisted on blocking the street and continued with their demonstration on 8 March 2005.
According to a report signed by eighteen police officers, when the demonstrators ignored the police and started marching, they blocked a main road.
In his report of 18 April 2005, the Malatya prosecutor expressed the opinion that the demonstrators had tried to break the police cordon and march on 8 March 2005.
Police officers dragged a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers sprayed the crowds with tear gas.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers hit some of the crowd, including four of the applicants.
The second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, was sprayed with tear gas during the events of 8 March 2005.
According to medical reports drawn up on 8 March 2005, the four applicants who had been hit by police officers had a number of injuries on their bodies.
According to medical reports drawn up on 8 March 2005, the injuries sustained by the four applicants rendered them unable to work for periods of between one and three days.
The part of the video footage where the police officers used force and arrested the applicants does not feature in the footage submitted to the Court.
The video footage resumes with the demonstrators protesting against the use of force by the police officers and asking for their arrested friends to be released.
It can be seen from the video footage that before they were arrested the applicants drew the police officers' attention to a circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004.
In the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004, the Ministry urges police officers to respect certain rights and freedoms, including freedom of expression and assembly.

In the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004, the Ministry reminds police officers that rights and freedoms including freedom of expression and assembly can only be restricted in limited circumstances.
In the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004, police officers are urged to show restraint when faced with demonstrations.
In the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004, police officers are urged to use their powers to promote the rights of civil society.

In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that in dispersing the unauthorised demonstration, the police officers had been impelled to resort to the use of force in order to apprehend the applicants because they had resisted arrest and insulted the police officers.
In their objection, the applicants argued that although they had not resisted arrest, the police officers had proceeded to arrest them by using force.
In their objection, the applicants pointed out that according to the applicable legislation, no prior permission was necessary to hold demonstrations.

The four applicants told the Malatya prosecutor on 8 March 2005 that before they could even begin their demonstration the police had arrested them without warning and, in the course of doing so, had hit them.
On 2 June 2005 the Malatya Criminal Court of First Instance acquitted the four applicants and the remaining defendants.
The Malatya Criminal Court of First Instance held on 2 June 2005 that there was no evidence to show that the four applicants had put up resistance against the police officers.

On 8 March 2005 the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, lodged an official complaint with the prosecutor against the police officers who, she alleged, had sprayed her and her daughter with tear gas.
On 8 March 2005 the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, orally informed the prosecutor that she would recognise the police officer who had sprayed her and her daughter with tear gas.

Approximately thirty-five days after 8 March 2005, the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, was asked by the investigating police officer whether she would be able to identify the police officer responsible for spraying her and her daughter with tear gas.

When asked approximately thirty-five days after the incident whether she could identify the police officer responsible, the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, stated that she had only seen him once and then only for a few seconds.
The second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, stated that had she been asked immediately after the incident she would have been able to recognise the police officer responsible.
On 11 March 2005 the remaining four applicants lodged an official complaint with the prosecutor against the police officers allegedly responsible for the ill-treatment.
On 16 March 2005 a police chief in Malatya sent a verbatim transcription of the video footage of the incidents to the Malatya prosecutor.
Between 4 April 2005 and 3 May 2005 the Malatya prosecutor took statements from eighteen police officers who had been on duty on the day of the incidents on 8 March 2005.

The remaining thirteen police officers' statements to the Malatya prosecutor concerned solely the complaints made by the applicants regarding the alleged assaults by male police officers on the way to the Malatya Court House.
The remaining thirteen police officers denied that the demonstrators had been assaulted in the police vehicles on 8 March 2005.
On 12 May 2005 the Malatya prosecutor decided not to prosecute the police officers involved in the events of 8 March 2005.
In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, had been unable to recognise the police officer who had sprayed her with tear gas.
In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that other than the applicants' unsubstantiated allegations, there was no evidence justifying the prosecution of the police officers.
The applicants lodged an objection against the Malatya prosecutor's decision of 12 May 2005 not to prosecute the police officers.
The objection filed by the applicants against the Malatya prosecutor's decision not to prosecute the police officers was rejected by the Elazığ Assize Court on 28 July 2005.
